title.en: Current assets and the operating cycle

body.en: An asset is current if it is expected to be realised within the operating cycle or 12 months, or is held for trading, or is cash. Operating cycle = time between acquiring assets for processing and their realisation in cash; if not identifiable, assume 12 months. *Current assets*: current investments, inventories (raw materials, WIP, finished goods, stock-in-trade, stores and spares, loose tools), trade receivables (debtors, bills receivable), cash and cash equivalents, short-term loans and advances, other current assets (prepaid expenses, accrued income).

problem.en: Find total current assets of Kapila Ltd.: Inventories ₹1,20,000; Debtors ₹60,000; Bills receivable ₹20,000; Cash at bank ₹40,000; Prepaid rent ₹10,000; Machinery ₹5,00,000.

steps.en: Machinery is property, plant and equipment, so it is excluded.

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. Find total current assets of Kapila Ltd.: Inventories 1,20,000 rupees; Debtors 60,000 rupees; Bills receivable 20,000 rupees; Cash at bank 40,000 rupees; Prepaid rent 10,000 rupees; Machinery 5,00,000 rupees.
Trade receivables equals Debtors 60,000 rupees plus Bills receivable 20,000 rupees equals 80,000 rupees.
Machinery is property, plant and equipment, so it is excluded.
Current assets equals 1,20,000 rupees plus 80,000 rupees plus 40,000 rupees plus 10,000 rupees equals 2,50,000 rupees.
So the answer is Total current assets 2,50,000 rupees.
